note: Teaching text, clarifying questions, inferred constraints and own examples. Inferred, not official. Examples are small boundary inputs with outputs from the independent references in oracles.py.

clarifyingQuestions: Does get refresh recency?
Is an entry exactly windowSize old still visible?
Are expired entries removed eagerly or count toward capacity?
hints: This is an LRU cache whose reads also check an age condition.
A hash map that remembers insertion order gives recency for free if you delete and re-insert on use.
On a successful get or any put, move the key to the end; evict from the front when size exceeds capacity.
invariants: map order is least to most recently used
size never exceeds capacity after put
chooseWhen: LRU semantics with an extra per-entry validity test
tradeoffs: Lazy expiry keeps code simple but lets stale keys occupy capacity
hack2hire:6778936c775a4a31045ead0e.variantLabel: Variant 1: LRU store with time-window reads

clarifyingQuestions: Is matching case-insensitive?
Can the header repeat a tag?
hints: Split on commas and trim spaces.
Keep supported tags in a set for O(1) membership.
Track emitted tags so repeats are skipped.
invariants: output has no duplicates
output order follows header order
tradeoffs: None material

clarifyingQuestions: Should a bare language match tags already returned?
In which order are a language's tags returned?
hints: A bare token has no hyphen.
Group supported tags by their first two letters, preserving supported order.
Skip tags already emitted.
invariants: each supported tag appears at most once
chooseWhen: Prefix matching over small tag lists
tradeoffs: Grouping costs a precomputation pass

clarifyingQuestions: Does * come last in practice or may it appear anywhere?
hints: * is just a token that matches everything.
Emit remaining tags in supported order.
An emitted set makes all three token kinds uniform.
invariants: each supported tag appears at most once
tradeoffs: None material

constraints: q in 0..1 with up to 3 decimals
clarifyingQuestions: Which token wins when several match one tag?
Is q=0 an explicit exclusion?
How are equal qualities ordered?
hints: Parse q into integer thousandths to avoid floats.
For each tag, the most specific matching token decides its quality.
Sort tags by (-q, earliest matching token, supported index).
invariants: quality comes from the most specific matching token
tradeoffs: Sorting adds log factor

clarifyingQuestions: Is the transferred amount rounded, and how?
Can a transaction mention an unknown account?
hints: Each transfer depends on the current balance, so order matters.
Simulate once and store results.
Use integer floor division to stay exact.
invariants: total money is conserved
tradeoffs: Precomputation holds all balances in memory

clarifyingQuestions: Is k a count of applied transactions or an index?
hints: Only two accounts change per transaction.
Record (step, newBalance) per changed account.
Binary search the last record with step <= k.
invariants: each account history is sorted by step
chooseWhen: Many historical reads over one fixed log
tradeoffs: Extra memory proportional to transactions

clarifyingQuestions: Ties ascending or descending by value?
hints: Count occurrences first.
Sort distinct values, not the full array.
Expand each value count times.
invariants: output is a permutation of items
tradeoffs: None material

clarifyingQuestions: Should the result be indices, heights or final totals?
hints: Only the two totals matter.
Compare totals before placing each ad; ties go left.
invariants: totals equal the sums of assigned heights
tradeoffs: Greedy is not globally balanced

clarifyingQuestions: How are ties between columns broken?
hints: You repeatedly need the smallest (total, index) pair.
A min-heap keyed by (total, column) gives it in O(log k).
Pop, assign, push back with the new total.
invariants: heap holds exactly one entry per column
tradeoffs: Heap overhead is wasted for k=2

constraints: 1..1e4 rows of printable ASCII up to 200 chars
up to 100 forbidden and ignore words [a-z0-9]{1,10}
clarifyingQuestions: What does each column mean and which rules apply?
Is the output the valid rows, the invalid rows or error messages?
Do duplicate ids count against invalid earlier rows?
hints: Validate each field independently, cheapest checks first.
Lowercase and tokenize once; forbidden and ignore lists become sets.
Track ids only from rows that passed every rule.
invariants: ids set contains exactly the ids of accepted rows
tradeoffs: Hand-written date validation avoids library differences between languages

clarifyingQuestions: What is the pay rate and unit?
Are canceled orders paid for time already spent?
Does concurrency change the rate?
hints: Pair each order's ACCEPTED and terminal record.
With a per-order rate, concurrency multiplies pay linearly, so per-order durations add.
invariants: pay is linear in total delivered minutes
tradeoffs: A sweep generalizes to non-linear concurrency pay at higher cost

constraints: ids and timestamps 0..1e9, logs up to 30 printable chars
clarifyingQuestions: Does a camera only see its own commands?
How do users receive logs?
Should polling block?
hints: Each camera needs its own FIFO.
Use an array plus head index (or deque) for O(1) pops.
invariants: commands for one camera leave in arrival order
tradeoffs: A sequential model cannot test locking

clarifyingQuestions: Are adjacent but non-overlapping ranges merged?
Is the output ids, messages or ranges?
hints: Convert ids to positions in the sorted list.
Each query becomes an index interval.
Sort intervals by start and merge when next start <= current end + 1.
invariants: merged intervals are disjoint and non-adjacent
tradeoffs: Sorting vs a coverage array: both linearithmic/linear

clarifyingQuestions: Can two pages disagree on content for one id?
hints: Every page is already sorted.
Keep the current head of each page in a min-heap.
Skip an id equal to the last one emitted.
invariants: emitted ids strictly increase
tradeoffs: Heap merge avoids a global sort but needs heap code in JS

clarifyingQuestions: How should unpriced services be handled?
What precision and rounding does the total use?
hints: Never parse money into floats.
Scale each rate to an integer number of 1e-4 dollars.
Round once at the end: (x + 50) // 100 cents.
invariants: running total is an exact integer in 1e-4 dollars
tradeoffs: JS needs BigInt for totals above 2**53

clarifyingQuestions: Are tiers applied per row or per service total?
Is a tier limit inclusive?
hints: Sum hours per service first.
Walk tiers, charging the hours that fall in each slice.
Keep everything in scaled integers.
invariants: charged hours across tiers sum to the service total
tradeoffs: Aggregation loses per-row attribution

clarifyingQuestions: Is the total the sum of rounded lines or the rounded exact sum?
How are lines ordered?
hints: Compute exact per-service costs before rounding.
Sort on the exact value, not the rounded string.
Round the total from the exact sum.
invariants: total is rounded once from the exact sum
tradeoffs: Line items may not add up to the total by a cent

clarifyingQuestions: What makes a name a directory?
hints: A dictionary from name to size covers every operation.
Check both endpoints before copying.
invariants: each name maps to exactly one size
tradeoffs: None material

clarifyingQuestions: How are equal sizes ordered?
Is there a result limit?
hints: Filter, then sort with a composite key.
invariants: output sorted by (-size, name)
tradeoffs: Linear scan per query; a trie would help only for prefixes

clarifyingQuestions: Who owns files added without a user?
Does a copy count against the owner's capacity?
What does merge return?
hints: Track used bytes per user incrementally.
Store the owner with each file.
Merge moves file ownership and adds capacities.
invariants: used[u] equals the size sum of files owned by u
tradeoffs: Owned-name sets cost memory but make merges proportional to moved files

clarifyingQuestions: What happens to files that conflict on restore?
Does merge transfer backups?
hints: A backup is a copied list of (name,size).
Restore = delete owned files, then re-add free names.
invariants: restore never overwrites another owner's file
tradeoffs: Full snapshots cost memory proportional to files

clarifyingQuestions: Are words with digits or uppercase letters snake case?
What about double or trailing underscores?
Inside string literals too?
hints: Work run by run, not character by character.
Strip leading underscores, then split on "_".
Reject runs with empty parts or uppercase letters.
invariants: non-identifier characters are copied verbatim
tradeoffs: No language-aware parsing, so string literals are rewritten too

clarifyingQuestions: Is greedy by fee rate acceptable or must it be optimal?
hints: Greedy by fee/size is not optimal for 0/1 choices.
dp[c] = best fee within capacity c.
Iterate capacities downward per item.
invariants: dp[c] is the best fee using processed items within capacity c
tradeoffs: Pseudo-polynomial in blockSize

clarifyingQuestions: Which optimal set should be returned on ties?
hints: Build best values over suffixes so earlier choices can be tested.
Include item i whenever doing so still reaches the optimum.
Compare (fee, -size) pairs.
invariants: the remaining optimum is reachable after every decision
chooseWhen: Need the witness, not just the value
tradeoffs: Full table costs n*B memory

clarifyingQuestions: Can a transaction have several parents?
hints: Order nodes in DFS preorder with subtree ends.
Skipping a node skips its whole subtree.
dp[i][c] = max(take i, jump to end of subtree).
invariants: a chosen node always has its parent chosen
tradeoffs: O(n*B) memory for the table

clarifyingQuestions: Are reverse rates implied (1/r)?
Can there be arbitrage cycles?
What precision is expected?
hints: Max product is a longest path in log space; without positive cycles it is well defined.
Relax edges V-1 times keeping the best product.
Keep products exact as integer / 10^(4k).
invariants: best[x] never decreases; at most V-1 rounds improve
tradeoffs: Big integers grow with path length

clarifyingQuestions: Is the threshold inclusive?
How are ties ordered?
hints: Only the referrer's total changes on a referred insert.
Keep (total,id) pairs sorted.
Binary search the first pair with total >= minTotal.
invariants: sorted list holds exactly one pair per customer
tradeoffs: Array insertion is O(n); a balanced tree would be O(log n)

clarifyingQuestions: Is depth 0 own revenue only?
hints: Store children of each customer.
BFS level by level and stop at maxDepth.
invariants: each customer visited at most once per query
tradeoffs: Per-query cost grows with subtree size

clarifyingQuestions: How are invalid moves reported?
Are columns 0- or 1-based?
hints: Only lines through the new disc can become wins.
Count same-colour discs both ways along each direction.
Win when count >= 4.

clarifyingQuestions: Does commit close only the innermost or all transactions?
What do rollback/commit return without a transaction?
hints: Snapshots are simple but copy the whole store.
Instead log the previous value of each key changed inside a transaction.
Maintain value counts incrementally on every write and undo.

Must phrase words be consecutive?
Result order?
